structuredContent.text:
### `updateMany()`

`updateMany` updates a batch of existing database records in bulk and returns the number of updated records.

content.text:
`updateMany` won't work here. It applies one `data` object to every row that matches `where`, so it can't give two rows different values. Instead, run two separate `update` calls in one `$transaction([...])`, so both succeed or both fail:

```ts
await prisma.$transaction([
  prisma.todoGroup.update({ where: { id: groupA.id }, data: { order: 2 } }),
  prisma.todoGroup.update({ where: { id: groupB.id }, data: { order: 1 } }),
]);
```

The docs describe `$transaction([])` for independent writes, and their example uses `updateMany` only to set the same value on many rows. I didn't find a docs example of swapping two values. The swap pattern above is my own suggestion, based on the `$transaction([])` API.

Sources:
- `apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v7/reference/prisma-client-reference.mdx`, "Model queries › updateMany()" (lines 1160–1162)
- `apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v7/prisma-client/queries/transactions.mdx`, "Independent writes › Scenario: Marking emails as read" (lines 345–382)
